anomaly_def.Name: MVCC Version Maintenance Anomaly + Replication Synchronization Anomaly + Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
MVCC Version Maintenance Anomaly : Excessive accumulation of obsolete row versions and rollback data because background cleanup cannot keep pace with update-/delete-driven churn.
Replication Synchronization Anomaly : Standby or subscriber nodes fall behind because they cannot receive, write, or apply the primary’s WAL/redo stream at its production rate.
Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly : The physical storage layer is saturated, driving up read/write latency and queue depth for data, log, and temporary files.

When all three faults are active, the system exhibits a compound symptom set: version stores, rollback segments, and table bloat expand rapidly while replica lag grows and primary log segments pile up, inflating disk-space usage. Autovacuum or purge workers and replica apply threads contend for the same over-burdened I/O subsystem, so both visibility-map scans and redo replays slow sharply. Checkpoints, sequential scans, and large deletes stretch far longer; replica read freshness degrades from seconds to minutes or hours; failovers risk data loss because the replica’s recovery point trails the primary’s transaction-ID horizon; meanwhile the primary warns of imminent wraparound yet cannot recycle WAL because lagging replicas still need it. Global performance shows high I/O wait, moderate CPU, swollen disk queues, and an accelerating feedback loop of bloat → more I/O → deeper lag.

Causally, heavy update/delete activity inflates the version store, forcing more page writes and generating extra WAL. The surge in log volume must traverse the replication channel, but limited network, CPU, or single-threaded apply logic on the replica slows consumption, so WAL accumulates on the primary. Retention of these log segments and the growing on-disk tables/indexes both expand the storage footprint, pushing the underlying disk array to its throughput limit. Elevated I/O latency then throttles autovacuum/purge and replica apply even further, allowing yet more dead tuples and WAL to gather. This positive feedback loop ties together MVCC cleanup debt, replication backlog, and storage saturation, creating a self-reinforcing degradation that can culminate in transaction-ID exhaustion, replica desynchronization, and service-level breaches.

entry.official_definition: Read timeout for X Plugin network communication.
entry.trigger_condition: A MySQL X Protocol read operation exceeds mysqlx_read_timeout.
entry.workload_impact: The X Protocol network read operation times out.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL X Plugin system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when network data is not acknowledged, received, or written within the configured transport-level waiting window.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect packet loss, transport latency, client responsiveness, proxy behavior, and whether slow consumers or unstable links are delaying network progress.
